criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: The student clearly states the primary mission (fluid lensing monitoring of Great Barrier Reef coral bleaching), the rationale/need, why only a single satellite is selected, and identifies operators and customer agencies (CSIRO, BOM).

evidence.quote: The satellite, nicknamed ZYZZsat (Z-axis/Y-axis Zeroed Zoning Satellite), is operated and accessed from Australia ground facilities, and is designed specifically for use above the Great Barrier Reef.
The ZYZZsat however, does not require such constant coverage as the reef bleaching events occur over days and weeks. Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Major design requirements are addressed (Vega E/CSG Kourou, SSO parameters, Mt Pleasant ground station access using STK, drag sail EOL, 5-year duration). overall: The submission presents a solid, well-conceived Australian Earth observation concept targeting coral bleaching with good STK access modelling. However, figure numbering and captions are absent, an incomplete sentence disrupts the EOL discussion, and Wikipedia is cited despite explicit task prohibition.

feedback.summary: You developed a strong, relevant Australian Earth observation mission concept targeting coral bleaching with solid initial STK modelling. Your introduction and conclusion effectively set and synthesised the mission context. To elevate your work, you need to expand your quantitative orbital design—particularly manoeuvre budgeting, reef coverage analysis, and deorbit sizing—while ensuring formal figure numbering, complete text editing, and strict adherence to academic sourcing guidelines.
next_steps: Perform quantitative orbital manoeuvre calculations and drag sail sizing to prove compliance with the 25-year post-mission disposal rule.
Include dedicated STK coverage figures and access statistics for the Great Barrier Reef target area, submitting the underlying scenario files.
Apply formal engineering presentation by numbering and captioning all figures and replacing informal sources (such as Wikipedia) with primary literature.

criteria.C1: You excellently detailed the mission rationale, target users (CSIRO, BOM), and justified a single-satellite architecture in the Introduction. To sustain this top level, ensure all design parameters are fully cross-referenced to primary literature.
criteria.C2: Your SSO selection and Mt Pleasant access analysis are well conceived. To reach Accomplished, avoid incomplete text in 'Mission Duration & EOL', provide quantitative drag sail sizing for the 25-year deorbit guideline, evaluate orbital manoeuvres, and include target coverage analysis.
criteria.C3: You delivered an appropriate synthesis in the Conclusion, connecting your operational selections back to the bleaching monitoring objectives. To progress further, incorporate specific quantitative performance outcomes directly into your closing summary.
criteria.C4: Your structure and contents page are good. To achieve an Accomplished standard, use formal figure numbering and captions rather than standalone titles, complete truncated sentences, and replace unapproved references like Wikipedia with peer-reviewed or official industry sources.
